title: Speedy's support for his travel and the Brussels night
summary: Speedy encouraged Jones to tour; on an Ellington tour he went out with Mercer and Edward Ellington instead of going straight to Paris.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: We just said, 'Well, let's take a chance at it.' And it worked. And she was not at all jealous of me being around the house. Say for instance the first time I went to Europe, she told me -- this was after I came out of the tuberculosis hospital -- she says, 'You go.' She would always encourage me to do things like that.
You know, a lot of wives wouldn't do it that way, you know. So when she was sick, later on with -- when I was with Ella, and the doctors told me that -- don't leave her alone, you know?

So I told her to meet me in Paris, and we'd been up in Scandinavia, we'd had a lot of fun and everything, you know, and she always used to kid me about the -- when the young ladies would make mistakes and call up my house.
And I had to break up laughing, and she'd look at me and laugh.

She'd say, 'I caught you again, didn't I?' So -- I'm going to back into another Ellington story that young Edward told me. So we were coming out of -- she was to meet me in Paris, and we were coming out of Brussels and we had a great show there, and you know, as you walk out of the side door, the stage door, Cootie and Duke turned like maybe right, and they wound up in a restaurant, and Mercer and Edward and I turned left and wound up in a swinging nightclub with a lot of pretty ladies there, you know? Now, we're due to be in Paris the next day, the next night, and oh we had a wonderful time, and we missed the morning plane. When we got there I picked her up at Orly Airport, and we didn't have to work that night. Everybody was there waiting for us, you know.
